name: Alvir photographic material study
source: User-supplied Alvir — 3D Model Project.pdf; extracted reference IDs in references/user-pdf/manifest.json
scope: Material and color interpretation only. No building-to-photo registration, measured heights, new landmark locations, or geometric corrections are claimed.
color_space: Artist-selected linear RGB shader values, visually guided by photographs; not calibrated reflectance measurements.
observations: Sandy earthen walls show broad uneven patches, exposed adobe and fine branching cracks.
Older construction coexists with exposed brick, grey cement and newer pale plaster; do not assign adobe to every building.
Faded sage-green gates, dark ironwork and weathered timber are stronger close-up references than uniformly saturated turquoise trim.
Dirt and gravel lanes coexist with modern asphalt streets; retain both.
Mature leafy shade is visible in the older lanes, but tree positions and canopy geometry have not been matched to the map.
Projecting timber roof ends and small openings are documented typologies, not measurements for existing modeled houses.

evidence_exclusions.002: PDF describes embedded aerial as a regional IRIB view; not a verified Alvir building-layout reference.
evidence_exclusions.003: Embedded image does not match the bare-tree description on page 5; ignore that scene/date attribution.
evidence_exclusions.040: Intact tower caption is not geolocated; do not reconstruct an Alvir tower from this image.

season: Maintain a coherent existing season. Green spring fields and dry fully-leafed scenes are different appearances, not evidence to make the entire landscape uniformly lush.
capture_dates: The date photos were sent is not their capture date. PDF dates and captions remain source claims.
